Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 226 - Misleading actions
sources.summary: When false or deceptive information, or a breach of a code commitment, makes a commercial practice a misleading action.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 227 - Misleading omissions
sources.summary: When omitting, hiding or obscuring material information makes a commercial practice a misleading omission, and what counts as material information.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 228 - Aggressive practices
sources.summary: When harassment, coercion or undue influence makes a commercial practice aggressive.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 229 - Contravention of the requirements of professional diligence
sources.summary: The standard of special skill and care a trader owes consumers in its field of activity.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 230 - Omission of material information from invitation to purchase
sources.summary: The listed information an invitation to purchase must carry, including the total price and the trader's identity and contact details.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 245 - Meaning of transactional decision
sources.summary: The decisions by a consumer that count as transactional decisions for the unfair commercial practices prohibition.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 246 - Meaning of average consumer: general
sources.summary: The average consumer benchmark against which the effect of a commercial practice is judged.

sources.title: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 section 248 - Meaning of product
sources.summary: What counts as a product, including services, digital content and rights or obligations.

sources.title: Consumer Rights Act 2015 section 62 - Requirement for contract terms and notices to be fair
sources.summary: The fairness test for consumer contract terms and notices, and the effect of an unfair term.

sources.title: Consumer Rights Act 2015 section 64 - Exclusion from assessment of fairness
sources.summary: When a term about the main subject matter or the price escapes the fairness assessment, conditional on transparency and prominence.

sources.title: Consumer Rights Act 2015 section 68 - Requirement for transparency
sources.summary: The duty to express written consumer contract terms and notices in plain and intelligible language, and legibly.

sources.title: Consumer Rights Act 2015 Schedule 2 - Consumer contract terms which may be regarded as unfair
sources.summary: The indicative grey list of consumer contract terms that may be regarded as unfair.

sources.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 regulation 9 - Information to be provided before making an on-premises contract
sources.summary: The pre-contract information a trader must give before an on-premises consumer contract is made.

sources.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 regulation 10 - Information to be provided before making an off-premises contract
sources.summary: The pre-contract information a trader must give on a durable medium before an off-premises consumer contract is made.

sources.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 regulation 13 - Information to be provided before making a distance contract
sources.summary: The pre-contract information a trader must give before a distance consumer contract is made, and how it binds the contract.

sources.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 regulation 19 - Offence relating to the failure to give notice of the right to cancel
sources.summary: The criminal offence a trader commits by not giving notice of the right to cancel an off-premises contract.

sources.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 Schedule 1 - Information relating to on-premises contracts
sources.summary: The listed pre-contract information for on-premises contracts referred to by regulation 9(1).

sources.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 Schedule 2 - Information relating to distance and off-premises contracts
sources.summary: The listed pre-contract information for distance and off-premises contracts referred to by regulations 10(1) and 13(1).

sources.title: Electronic Commerce (EC Directive) Regulations 2002 regulation 6 - General information to be provided by a person providing an information society service
sources.summary: The identifying and pricing information an online service provider must make available to recipients.

sources.title: Electronic Commerce (EC Directive) Regulations 2002 regulation 17 - Mere conduit
sources.summary: The liability shield for an intermediary that only transmits or provides access to information.

sources.title: Electronic Commerce (EC Directive) Regulations 2002 regulation 18 - Caching
sources.summary: The liability shield for automatic, intermediate and temporary storage of transmitted information.

sources.title: Electronic Commerce (EC Directive) Regulations 2002 regulation 19 - Hosting
sources.summary: The liability shield for storing information provided by a recipient of the service, and the actual-knowledge condition that removes it.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 24 - Responsibility of the controller
sources.summary: The controller's general obligation to implement, review and update measures that ensure and demonstrate that processing complies with the Regulation.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 45 - Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision
sources.summary: Adequacy-decision transfers, omitted on 5 February 2026 by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025. Mirrored so it is not cited as live; Article 45A now carries approval by regulations.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 45A - Transfers approved by regulations
sources.summary: The Secretary of State's power to approve transfers to a third country or international organisation by regulations, subject to the data protection test.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 45B - The data protection test
sources.summary: The not-materially-lower standard a third country or international organisation must meet before transfers to it are approved by regulations.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 46 - Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
sources.summary: The appropriate-safeguards route for a restricted transfer, listing binding corporate rules and the standard data protection clauses issued by the Commissioner under section 119A of the Data Protection Act 2018.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 47 - Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards: Binding corporate rules
sources.summary: What binding corporate rules must contain before the Commissioner approves them as appropriate safeguards for intra-group transfers.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 47A - Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards: further provision
sources.summary: The Secretary of State's power to specify standard data protection clauses and further safeguards relied on for transfers under Article 46.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 49 - Derogations for specific situations
sources.summary: The derogations, including explicit consent and contract necessity, that permit a restricted transfer where neither approval by regulations nor appropriate safeguards apply.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 49A - Restriction in the public interest
sources.summary: The Secretary of State's power to restrict transfers of a category of personal data to a third country for important reasons of public interest.

sources.title: DPA 2018 section 119A - Standard clauses for transfers to third countries etc
sources.summary: The Commissioner's power to issue standard data protection clauses for restricted transfers, which is the statutory basis of the International Data Transfer Agreement and the UK Addendum to the EU standard contractual clauses.

sources.citation: ICO contracts and liabilities between controllers and processors
sources.title: Contracts and liabilities between controllers and processors
sources.summary: What details about the processing an Article 28(3) contract must set out, the minimum required terms including processing only on the controller's documented instructions, and the point at which a processor that acts outside those instructions becomes a controller.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 on the concepts of controller and processor in the GDPR
sources.summary: How specific an Article 28(3) contract must be about the type of personal data and the categories of data subject, and the documented instructions boundary at which a processor becomes a controller. EU guidance, persuasive only in the United Kingdom.
